head_commit.message:
T-3030: Glessner's stable hoist stone as its 4 ft cantilever, cupola ledges wrapped (#1204)

The c. 1887 Cornell view sees the hoist stone's west side face from the
northwest: through its solved camera (local offset at the arch's crown
removed) the side runs 62 px from wall to nose, which a 4.0 ft projection
gives (1.75 ft gives 27). Its end face reads 0.75 ft wide and 0.83 ft deep.
HABS 01 puts the nose where a 3-4 ft projection does; its long dark band
along the wall is the stone's cast shadow, not a beam. HABS 15 sees the lit
sloping underside (about 42 px, a 3.6 ft projection) and the foot about
10 px lower. So: W 140.75-141.5, foot 26.0 ft, top 28.15 ft, 4.0 ft out,
0.83 ft nose (new optional `nose_ft`). Both northwest prints run the
cupola's landing ledges unbroken round its corners; they now wrap
(`ledge_corners: wrapped`, opt-in, no other building changes).

Rebaked glessner_house (archive repacked, K01 baseline re-measured,
source-use coverage rebuilt); the three stable-end match records reviewed
and kept `differs` with what stays open. The cupola's height is split out
as T-3031 (Cornell and HABS 01 disagree on it). L-glessner-hoist-3030.

head_commit.message:
T-3017: 1904 parkway elms grow as open-grown American elms; leaf cards cut to their leaves (#1199)

The parkway elm drew as one straight bole under a round crown, and at the
street's mid level every leaf clump was one card of the massed-clump tile,
a fan of sprays, which the owner saw as "fans of leaves and not branches".

- tree-model.js: ARCH.ulmus_americana_vase and growElm: clear bole to about a
  third, 2-4 co-dominant stems that fork again and arch out, branches sweeping
  out and down, hanging twigs; leaf as sprays hung from the twigs and faced to
  the street and the ground; every child grows from its parent's wood.
- Every grown tree's leaf card is cut to its tile's opaque box (LEAF_CROP,
  printed by generate_tree_atlas.py --crops): same leaves in the same place,
  about 30% less card area for the GPU to shade and alpha-test.
- Phone tier (`coarse`): fewer, larger sprays and no sub-pixel branches; the
  phone's distant ring for the elms comes in to 220 m.
- Liberty L-elm-vase-3017, changelog entry.

head_commit.message:
T-3020: 1736 Prairie's card stops showing the other McBirney house (#1201)

* T-3020: 1736 Prairie's card stops showing the other McBirney house

The January 1890 Inland Architect plate "Residence for Hugh J. McBirney" is the
son's Tudor stone house at 1625 Prairie. Its library record still listed the
Art Institute's wrong catalogue address (1736) under addresses, and the library
places a record on every lot its addresses name, so the plate sat on 1736's
lot: at the top of 1736's card and in its structure grade. The address is
dropped (the notes keep why). The June 1889 American Architect permit for
H. J. McBirney's three-storey Burling & Whitehouse dwelling is the same 1625
house and moves there too. 1736's model was built from its own c. 1890
photograph and is unchanged.

Rebuilding images.json also folds in library edits other PRs left unbuilt:
the three 2013 Glessner capital close-ups (now with their evidence reviews and
image-store entries) and three Glessner record edits; site-plan.json
re-derives from the current street grid. Sidecar grades and the built-so-far
walk re-derive.

head_commit.message:
T-3006: K01 rounds a corner; 1811 Prairie's entrance block turned on 0.9 m from the 1888 plate (#1196)

* T-3006: K01 rounds a corner; 1811 Prairie's entrance block turned on 0.9 m from the 1888 plate

K01 learns round_corner: a quarter round tangent to the street front and its side
wall, coursed on the front's own beds in its stone and curved stone by stone, with
a dressed corbel in its last course squaring it out under the cornice, eave and
coped gable. 1811's south corner (K01's 'north') is laid on it at 0.9 m, and its
corner downpipe stands on the round where the plate draws it. Every other K01,
K12, K13 and K16 asset re-emits byte-identical; only inputs_sha256 moved.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* T-3006: hold round_corner with its own test; the all-stone rule reads the round as the front's

tools/test_k01_round_corner.py builds 1811's round and refuses a radius past a
quarter of the block, an unknown key or corner, a pipe before the front's plane
over the round or buried in it, a pipe behind the flat front, a bay on the round
and a round with no stone front; check.sh runs it beside the other K01 tests.
A pipe on the round now stands as far off the curve as a front pipe stands off
the front. check_stone_house_kit's as-was rule no longer reads the round, the
street front's own stone turning the corner, as a stone flank.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* T-3006: rebuild the plate's source-use backlinks and measure the round corner's test step

compile_source_use.py: 1811's round_corner cites the 1888 plate, so the plate's
backlinks and the coverage page move. measure_step_isolation.mjs --tool: the new
test_k01_round_corner.py step writes nothing in-tree.
